column10: In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes rather than two. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- leaves .failcount untouched and KEEPS the queued successor, which is the resume itself. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor, which would repeat it. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, and an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed, so the only storage numbers in force are budget.env's. codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh no longer names the TensorFlow-era exporter anywhere. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the first row are unchanged. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume; that is by design and its executed proof is o25's. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATIONS (reproduced, recorded as o33 and o34, not repaired here): (1) SCHED_TERM outranks every class except the deliberate storage stop, so a SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight, or after the loop has already failed but before finalize runs, is booked as a scheduler termination with the count untouched and the successor kept; the wrapper does not consult SCHED_TERM before launching the loop, so a link signalled during its pre-flight still starts the loop (offline it ran to completion; on the cluster SIGKILL follows KillWait 30 s later). (2) A loop status 143 after KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS is booked as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, KTG_MAX_FAILS and KTG_MAX_CHAIN read the job environment, which Slurm's default --export=ALL propagates down the chain. (3) Because a healthy production link never exits 0 (the loop is open-ended), .failcount never decays: KTG_MAX_FAILS=3 means three failures over the chain's lifetime, not three consecutive links (scenario O). (4) loop.sbatch:455 launches the loop as `bash "$LOOP_SH"`, so the loop script's shebang options `#!/bin/bash -eu` are inert; errexit is active only from synchronous_loop_9x9.sh:232 (after the first cycle's guard call) and nounset never, so the archive-staging section :44-228 runs unguarded under the wrapper, contrary to the script's header comment :11-12.

column10: Counterexample to the premise of tasks/paper_code_map_search section 2 (a) that a cheap turn logs exactly Root visits: 100 and a full turn up to 600, so that '> 100' identifies a full search. On the fork-free 60-game run the root-visit histogram is 100 x 4872, 600 x 1862 and 667 values strictly between (101..586, 322 distinct), identical between the engine log (7401 lines) and the sgf per-move annotations (7401 moves over 60 games, one per searched turn). The '> 100' rule gives (7401 - 4872)/7401 = 0.34171, exactly the number in probe_search_nofork-299259.json; 'Root visits == maxVisits' gives 1862/7401 = 0.25159. Mechanism, from the reference code: a fresh cheap search stops at exactly 100 visits and a fresh full search at exactly 600 because cpp/search/search.cpp:509,579-580 count the reused root visits (numNonPlayoutVisits) toward maxVisits; selfplay clears the tree before every full search (cpp/program/play.cpp:1567 asserts clearBotBeforeSearch for forSelfPlay, :1234 clears) but NOT before a cheap search when cheapSearchTargetWeight <= 0 (play.cpp:1147), so a cheap search that inherits a subtree already holding >= 100 visits does zero new playouts and logs the inherited count. The mechanism's sharp prediction -- a between value can only follow a 600 or another between value in the same game, never a 100, and never opens a game -- holds exactly: 0 of 667 follow a 100, 533 follow a 600, 134 follow a between, 0 open a game. The other candidate mechanisms are excluded: 'Total games: 78' is 60 games run plus 18 game threads that each did one fetch_add past -max-games-total and ran nothing (cpp/command/selfplay.cpp:292-293; the log has exactly 60 'Started' lines and 18 'terminating' lines, and 7401 log lines = 7401 sgf moves, so no in-flight game contributes); reanalysis is off (useReanalyze absent, cpp/program/playsettings.cpp:110) and side positions do not call logSearch; sekiForkHackProb cannot produce a third visit value. Independent second run: the smoke loop's own 80 random-net games (reduceVisits=true, forks at cfg values, a different net and job) give 2311/9211 = 0.25090 at v == 600 and 0 of 543 between values after a 100. Consequences: the 0.333 / 0.344 / 0.342 in the three probe rows are artefact values of one instrument, so the band [0.20, 0.30] is NOT refuted; it is also NOT admitted here, because the task-file criterion is defined through the defective rule and the two 20-game rows cannot be re-binned (the probe script's rm -rf removed their logs, sgfs and npz). The validator records 0.25159 and 0.25090 as observations and proposes no band; the positive measurement is the worker's to re-propose under a corrected discriminator (o38).

column4: Slurm chain wrapper + mission loop copy: errexit in force however the loop is launched, every process-internal exit accounted, the scheduler's own termination told apart from a cycle and from a failure, and the three pre-launch wirings the chain needs -- declared CPUs read from the knob file and asserted, the stage sampler running for the whole link, and a pre-shuffle pos_len guard (static + offline injection)
column10: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. column10: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATION (o36): that holds for every VALUE a state file can hold, and a corrupt .failcount costs at most one extra link because finalize() overwrites it with a plain decimal on the next failure (harness X8: abc, then 2, then 4 and the breaker on link 2; X8b at the slow-failure floor trips on link 3; X9: the corrupt value persists only across scheduler-terminated links, with a WARNING each). It does NOT hold when the file cannot be WRITTEN: no write of .failcount or .chain_depth is checked, so a .failcount that is a directory, unreadable or read-only is read as 0 (no WARNING when cat fails) and never advances -- every link prints 'chain continues' and queues its successor, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN (X3, X4, X5); the same fail-open direction applies to the operator knobs, which are not read through read_counter: KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test false so the breaker never trips (X10b: 2, 4, 6 with a successor each link) and KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound (X10c); KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual). The loop's own CHANGE 10 writer carries the same trim / guard / width / 10# parse, so a seeded 08 self-heals to 9 on the next completed cycle instead of killing the loop after every cycle. No writer in codes/ can produce a padded value in the first place (no printf %0Nd, no seq -w; every write is an unpadded $(( )) result), so the exposure only ever needed a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Nothing here ran on a GPU or under a real scheduler. AMENDMENT (wave 3, R1/R6/R5). loop.sbatch:8 declares --cpus-per-task=32; the wrapper types no CPU count at all -- REQ_CPUS is KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK read from codes/loop/knobs_9x9.env, whose sha256 is logged at pre-flight; a knob file that is unreadable, or that carries KTG_MAX_FAILS/KTG_MAX_CHAIN/KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, is not sourced at all, resubmit() then refuses to chain and the pre-flight exits 2; a granted SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK != KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK, or either engine cfg declaring a numGameThreads != KTG_NUM_GAME_THREADS, is a pre-flight failure (exit 2) that cancels the queued successor. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATIONS (2026-09-04, record results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/wave3_prelaunch_repairs/validation.md). (i) The stray-knob guard is a line-anchored grep for NAME= at the start of a line: a knob file carrying a plain KTG_MAX_FAILS= / KTG_MAX_CHAIN= / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS= assignment is refused before sourcing (V1f, V1i), but the spelling export KTG_MAX_FAILS=1 is sourced and retunes the breaker for that link (V1g: failcount 0/1, breaker on the first failure), and a $NAME reference to an unset variable anywhere in the knob file aborts the wrapper at :186 under set -u BEFORE the resubmit and BEFORE the EXIT trap, so that link ends with no successor and no accounting (V1j, the o26 class); both need an edit of the knob file, whose every non-comment line at HEAD is NAME=digits with no $ (o42). (ii) stage_monitor.sh stop kills the pids listed in monitor.pids without checking what they are: after a SIGKILLed link (no finalize, monitor.run and monitor.pids left behind, V6e) a successor that fails its pre-flight BEFORE its own start runs stop from finalize on the stale pids and kills whatever same-user process now holds them (V6g: an unrelated sleep of this user was killed); a successor that reaches start overwrites both files first. (iii) The pos_len guard is an mtime test: a file whose mtime predates the marker (rsync -a / cp -p onto a resumed tree, V5e) or a marker whose mtime is in the future (clock skew, V5f) is skipped until the marker is removed, and a file written between the pre-shuffle check and the shuffle (V5k) is shuffled unguarded that cycle and refused at the next link's loop-start check; the guard costs 0.53 s for 400 npz (V5g). A candidate may be a comma-joined Slurm partition set ("b200,l40s"), whose free-GPU count is summed over its members because sinfo -p takes the same comma list; comma is Slurm's spelling and never a candidate separator. The decided behaviour, documented in the file, is "b300 when it has a free GPU and no reservation or drain blocks it, otherwise the multi-partition set". resubmit() passes that resolved string unchanged to both the compute-budget pre-flight and sbatch, and KTG_PARTITIONS reaches every successor on the same path as KTG_MAX_CHAIN / KTG_MAX_FAILS / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- a plain ${VAR:-default} assignment plus an sbatch call with no --export of its own, so Slurm's default --export=ALL applies. column4: Slurm chain wrapper + mission loop copy: errexit in force however the loop is launched, every process-internal exit accounted, the scheduler's own termination told apart from a cycle and from a failure, a partition candidate set the whole chain inherits, and a successor id that survives the site's own stderr banner so the queued successor stays cancellable (static + offline injection)
column10: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATION (o36): that holds for every VALUE a state file can hold, and a corrupt .failcount costs at most one extra link because finalize() overwrites it with a plain decimal on the next failure (harness X8: abc, then 2, then 4 and the breaker on link 2; X8b at the slow-failure floor trips on link 3; X9: the corrupt value persists only across scheduler-terminated links, with a WARNING each). It does NOT hold when the file cannot be WRITTEN: no write of .failcount or .chain_depth is checked, so a .failcount that is a directory, unreadable or read-only is read as 0 (no WARNING when cat fails) and never advances -- every link prints 'chain continues' and queues its successor, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN (X3, X4, X5); the same fail-open direction applies to the operator knobs, which are not read through read_counter: KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test false so the breaker never trips (X10b: 2, 4, 6 with a successor each link) and KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound (X10c); KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual). The loop's own CHANGE 10 writer carries the same trim / guard / width / 10# parse, so a seeded 08 self-heals to 9 on the next completed cycle instead of killing the loop after every cycle. No writer in codes/ can produce a padded value in the first place (no printf %0Nd, no seq -w; every write is an unpadded $(( )) result), so the exposure only ever needed a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Nothing here ran on a GPU or under a real scheduler. AMENDMENT (wave 3, R1/R6/R5). loop.sbatch:8 declares --cpus-per-task=32; the wrapper types no CPU count at all -- REQ_CPUS is KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK read from codes/loop/knobs_9x9.env, whose sha256 is logged at pre-flight; a knob file that is unreadable, or that carries KTG_MAX_FAILS/KTG_MAX_CHAIN/KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, is not sourced at all, resubmit() then refuses to chain and the pre-flight exits 2; a granted SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK != KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK, or either engine cfg declaring a numGameThreads != KTG_NUM_GAME_THREADS, is a pre-flight failure (exit 2) that cancels the queued successor. The policy script named by mission.json compute.policyCheck passes at --gpus 1 --cpus 32 --partition b200. loop.sbatch starts codes/eval/stage_monitor.sh over $BASEDIR/monitor with its own pid as the sampling root after env.sh and the knob asserts (a missing sampler is a pre-flight failure), and stops it as the first statement of finalize() after FINALIZED=1, || true; synchronous_loop_9x9.sh retags the samples cycleN at the top of each cycle when $BASEDIR/monitor/monitor.run exists. The link samples at KTG_MON_PS_INTERVAL=1 / KTG_MON_GPU_INTERVAL=5; stage_monitor.sh's own defaults stay the smoke's 0.2 s / 2 s. synchronous_loop_9x9.sh runs codes/eval/check_pos_len_npz.py at loop start and again between selfplay and shuffle in every cycle, over the npz under $BASEDIR/selfplay newer than $BASEDIR/.pos_len_checked (all of them when the marker is absent), skipping cleanly at 0 files and touching the marker after a pass; a mismatch names the file and ends the cycle with exit 1 BEFORE the shuffle, instead of the train-time assert at data_processing_pytorch.py:91 a whole selfplay stage later. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATIONS (2026-09-04, record results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/wave3_prelaunch_repairs/validation.md). (i) The stray-knob guard is a line-anchored grep for NAME= at the start of a line: a knob file carrying a plain KTG_MAX_FAILS= / KTG_MAX_CHAIN= / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS= assignment is refused before sourcing (V1f, V1i), but the spelling export KTG_MAX_FAILS=1 is sourced and retunes the breaker for that link (V1g: failcount 0/1, breaker on the first failure), and a $NAME reference to an unset variable anywhere in the knob file aborts the wrapper at :186 under set -u BEFORE the resubmit and BEFORE the EXIT trap, so that link ends with no successor and no accounting (V1j, the o26 class); both need an edit of the knob file, whose every non-comment line at HEAD is NAME=digits with no $ (o42). (ii) stage_monitor.sh stop kills the pids listed in monitor.pids without checking what they are: after a SIGKILLed link (no finalize, monitor.run and monitor.pids left behind, V6e) a successor that fails its pre-flight BEFORE its own start runs stop from finalize on the stale pids and kills whatever same-user process now holds them (V6g: an unrelated sleep of this user was killed); a successor that reaches start overwrites both files first. Needs SIGKILL plus a deterministic pre-flight failure plus pid reuse by a same-user process; bounded to one kill; recorded as o42 (b). (iii) The pos_len guard is an mtime test: a file whose mtime predates the marker (rsync -a / cp -p onto a resumed tree, V5e) or a marker whose mtime is in the future (clock skew, V5f) is skipped until the marker is removed, and a file written between the pre-shuffle check and the shuffle (V5k) is shuffled unguarded that cycle and refused at the next link's loop-start check; the guard costs 0.53 s for 400 npz (V5g). (iv) The sampler survives no end of a link: a process-group SIGTERM (walltime form, V6c) ends it, a wrapper-only SIGTERM leaves it to finalize's stop (V6d, 35 samples, 0 alive after), a SIGKILL leaves the run file behind but the samplers end on kill -0 of the dead root within one interval (V6e, 0 alive after 3 s); its cost is about 6 % of one core at 1 s on a 1751-process login node (90 ms per ps sweep, V6j). (v) The dry run stages 87 files / 28880227 B, not the 80 / 28702024 B the task file cites: the scratch clone's python/katago and python/muon now carry 13 __pycache__ files that upstream's cp -r copies into every dated archive; before and after are byte-identical (manifest diff exit 0). (vi) The compare of SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is skipped when the variable is unset (V1c); that is not a hole in a real link because the batch environment of every job so far carried it (cfg9x9 job 298359 printed SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK = 24, both smoke jobs printed cpus_per_task = 24 from it) and job 299366 shows CPUs/Task=32. AMENDMENT (fifth repair, o44). pick_partition() no longer carries a hard-coded partition list: codes/loop/loop.sbatch:287 reads KTG_PARTITIONS, defaulting to the historical "b300 b200", and :288-303 tries those candidates in order and falls back to the LAST one rather than a literal b200. A candidate may be a comma-joined Slurm partition set ("b200,l40s"), whose free-GPU count is summed over its members because sinfo -p takes the same comma list; comma is Slurm's spelling and never a candidate separator. The decided behaviour, documented in the file, is "b300 when it has a free GPU and no reservation or drain blocks it, otherwise the multi-partition set". resubmit() passes that resolved string unchanged to both the compute-budget pre-flight and sbatch, and KTG_PARTITIONS reaches every successor on the same path as KTG_MAX_CHAIN / KTG_MAX_FAILS / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- a plain ${VAR:-default} assignment plus an sbatch call with no --export of its own, so Slurm's default --export=ALL applies. That closes the asymmetry the production_chain_9x9 launcher held at its pre-submission gate: a first link submitted --partition=b200,l40s used to queue links 2..9 on b300/b200 only. With the knob unset the function is byte-identical in behaviour to the pre-repair one over the whole b300 state matrix. NOT covered: the list is expanded unquoted, so a shell metacharacter in the knob globs against the job's cwd, and an unallowed candidate of any spelling is caught only by the compute-budget pre-flight, which refuses to chain rather than submitting; loop.sbatch still has no partition-consistency pre-flight of its own. THREE THINGS ARE NOT CLAIMED. (i) No cycle has executed at 1500 games -- the evidence is a derivation over production measurements plus an executed arithmetic check, not a measurement of the loop at this value. (ii) The lower bound is a HORIZON, not a resting point: at -0.1528 rows/game per accepted net the marginal reaches 16.0, where T1 fails again at 1500, after ~16.5 further accepted nets. A 20-net horizon at -0.1528 gives 15.47 < 16.0, so 1500 is NOT safe against twenty more accepted nets at the fitted slope; at either slope the marginal reaches 16.0 in ~16 accepted nets, which at the measured cadence (17 acceptances in 50 cycles) is ~47 cycles = 14-19 h at the 0.29-0.39 h/cycle expected at 1500 games -- INSIDE link 2's 23.5 h if the drift stays linear.
